senses.gloss: , Vav, name of the sixth letter of the Alphabet Kidd. 30ᵃ וא״ו דגחון חציין וכ׳ the Vav in Gaḥon (Lev. XI, 42) marks the (first) half of the number of letters in the Pentateuch.
units: Ib. וא״ו … מהאי גיסא וכ׳ does the Vav of gaḥon belong to the first half or to the second?—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 58:3">Gen. R. s. 58</cite> Ephron (<cite ref="Genesis 33:16">Gen. XXXIII, 16</cite>) is spelt <he>הסר וא״ו</he> without Vav; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:4:2">Y. Shebu. I, 33ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>ושעיר וי״ו מוסיף וכ׳</he> the Vav in Us’ir (<cite ref="Numbers 28:22">Num. XXVIII, 22</cite>) adds to the preceding subject, i.e. a goat in addition to &c.
Kidd. 66ᵇ וי״ו דשלום וכ׳ the Vav in Shalom (Num. XXV, 12) is curtailed (so that it may be read Shalem, unblemished).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 87a:17">B. Mets. 87ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Megillah 16b:10">Meg. 16ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="L00114"><he>לַבְרוּת</he></cite>.—

<cite ref="Yoma 45a:14">Yoma 45ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>וא״ו לא דרשי</he> they do not use the Vav for interpretation; a. fr.—Pl. <he>יָוִי״ם</he>, <he>וָוִי״ן</he>. Y. Meg. I, 71ᶜ top (deriving from <he>ווי העמודים</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 27:10">Ex. XXVII, 10</cite>) <he>שיהא ווים וכ׳</he> that the shape of the Vav in the Pentateuch is column-like (as in <he>כתב אשורית</he>); <cite ref="Sanhedrin 22a:5">Snh. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>מה … אף ווים וכ׳</he> as the columns have not changed (their shape), so has not the shape of the Vav.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 1:2:2">Y. Naz. I, 51ᵇ</cite> top <he>עד שיזכיר ו׳</he> he must utter the Vav conjunctive. Ib. IV, beg. 53ᵃ <he>מאן תאנא ו׳</he> who is it that says the Vav must be uttered?; Y. Kidd. II, 62ᵇ; a. fr.
